newsitem.title: INDIA: India markets run out of steam as euphoria wanes.
newsitem.headline: India markets run out of steam as euphoria wanes.

text.p: Profit-takers snapped a two-day winning streak in Indian shares on Thursday and analysts predicted a quieter trend.
After a sharp rise of 212 points or about 6.7 percent in the past two days, the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index dropped 90.92 points, or 2.72 percent, to 3,250.94.
"People are cautious. It will take some time for confidence to rebuild in the market," said a dealer at a brokerage firm.
The easier credit policy for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) announced last Saturday by the central bank met market expectations, but analysts said the euphoria was waning.

"Market sentiment turned positive after the central bank's favourable credit policy, but we haven't seen any fundamental changes in the economy," said Homiyar Vasania, head of research at Paragh Parikh Financial Advisory Services.
The reduction in interest rates by the Reserve Bank of India prompted some banks and term lending institutions to cut their prime lending rates by 0.5-1.0 one percentage point 14.5-16.5 percent.
Pivotals like bank major State Bank of India and steel giant Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO) which led the market rally bore the selling brunt on Thursday.
"The rise in share prices was just an illusion," Vasania said.
Shares of TISCO fell 6.75 rupees to 186.0 while SBI lost 14.20 rupees to 225.75.
"We have been expecting a correction, but it remains to be seen if this is a temporary reaction," said Manish Gupta, research analyst at Khandwala Securities, a local brokerage firm.
"The market was overheated. It's more of a sentiment-driven rally with the big guys (foreign institutional investors) not operating in a big way," Gupta said.
He said buying was limited to big cap stocks with little participation seen in the broader section.
